transcript:
Meeting header — 2026-10-27 16:00 UTC | Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Sam Collins (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Hale (CTO, Aegis), Dr. Lena Ortiz (Security Lead), Jamal Price (Cloud Architect), Sofia Nguyen (Legal).

[00:00] Sam Collins: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time. Quick goal for today: walk through our encryption posture questions, how BYOK/HSM would fit into Redwood, and any audit / compliance constraints you have.
[00:14] Marcus Hale: Yep thanks Sam. We've been re-evaluating key custody for flight control logs — need to be sure keys never leave our control, also residency for EU maintenance data.
[00:22] Dr. Lena Ortiz: And we need SOC2 alignment, plus some internal policy specifics around separation of duties — we want proof that key usage is auditable end-to-end.
[00:30] Sam Collins: Totally. Priya and I will outline the integration options: 1) Hosted KMS with tenant BYOK via customer-wrapped keys; 2) Dedicated HSM connector running in your VPC; 3) On-prem HSM with local gateway + periodic sync.
[00:45] Priya Nair: I'll add we're also mindful of latency — if you plan high-frequency inference on large payloads, avoiding remote unwraps per-request is important. So caching ephemeral data keys at the runtime level is typical, but you control the lifetime.
[01:03] Jamal Price: Quick clarification — when you say caching, is that the KV cache? how's that locked down?
[01:09] Priya Nair: Yeah that's the KV cache — sometimes transcribed as K V cache — basically the runtime keeps the decrypted KV in memory on the inference node for the duration of the session. It's encrypted at-rest on disk, and never written to persistent storage unless you opt in. We can configure TTLs and per-tenant segmentation.
[01:29] Dr. Lena Ortiz: What about key rotation? Our policy mandates rotation every 90 days and minimum key size 3072 RSA — does Redwood support those constraints?
[01:38] Sam Collins: We support configurable rotation windows. For BYOK with HSM-backed keys, rotation can be orchestrated in your KMS and Redwood will pick up new key versions via the connector. For RSA vs AES: most inference uses symmetric keys (AES-256) for data keys; RSA is typically used for key wrapping. We can accommodate your minimums with HSM-generated RSA when needed.
[02:04] Sofia Nguyen: Also to flag export control issues — we may not be able to have keys leave US jurisdiction for certain datasets. Is there an option to keep keys entirely in our HSM on-prem?
[02:13] Priya Nair: Yes, on-prem HSM + local gateway keeps keys in your control. Our private deployment supports a connector pattern: Redwood's control plane issues signed requests, but the unwrap happens in your environment. For hosted deployments we offer tenant BYOK where you provide wrapped key material — but that still requires an unwrap step in Redwood's dedicated runtime unless you use the HSM connector.
[02:38] Marcus Hale: Can you sketch the network topology quickly? ports, egress, etc — we have strict firewall rules.
[02:44] Sam Collins: Sure. I'll share a diagram after the call, but high level: HSM connector runs in your VPC, it listens on an internal port for signed unwrap requests from runtime shards. Outbound rules are minimal, mostly to the control plane for telemetry. We'll provide a port matrix and CIDR list.
[03:02] Jamal Price: Is the connector one-way? can it initiate connections only?
[03:06] Priya Nair: Connection is outbound from the runtime to your connector endpoint, mutual TLS. The connector performs the unwrap and returns the data key over the mTLS channel. We can also support a polling model if you prefer no inbound connectivity.
[03:24] Dr. Lena Ortiz: How are audit logs generated for key usage? We need immutable logs with signer identity and request payload hash.
[03:32] Sam Collins: We emit audit events for key usage: timestamp, tenant id, runtime shard id, key version id, operation type. When you use your HSM, audit entries still show the fact that the unwrap happened, and you get the HSM's audit trail on your side. For immutability, we recommend forwarding logs into your SIEM with signed append-only storage.
[03:54] Marcus Hale: Are these logs tamper-evident? We run regular attestation checks.
[03:58] Priya Nair: We can sign log bundles with a service-level signing key, and you can cross-check hashes. If you need hardware-backed log signing, we can coordinate a PKI handshake with your HSM.
[04:14] Jamal Price: Any performance numbers? say 512-token responses, 50 RPS — what's the added latency for an unwrap per request?
[04:20] Sam Collins: If you unwrap per request over a remote HSM, that could add 20–80ms depending on network and HSM. With a local connector and caching the data key in-memory for short TTLs, typical added latency is <5ms. For high RPS we recommend ephemeral data keys and runtime caching.
[04:42] Dr. Lena Ortiz: For compliance, do you maintain SOC 2 type II and ISO 27001?
[04:47] Sam Collins: Yes, Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and is ISO-attested. We can share the compliance pack; we'll need an NDA for some of the supporting artifacts.
[04:58] Sofia Nguyen: NDA is fine, but we also need contractual language for key escrow and breach notification timelines.
[05:04] Sam Collins: Understood — we have standard enterprise terms, but for BYOK and HSM we can include clauses that keys remain customer-managed and we only have a conduit role. We'll follow up with legal.
[05:16] Marcus Hale: On the HSM side, we use LunaNet appliances and a KMS that supports RFC 7515 for wrapping — any known incompatibilities?
[05:25] Priya Nair: We have connectors tested against common HSM vendors including Thales/Luna and AWS CloudHSM. For RFC 7515 (JWE/JWS) wrapping, we'll validate the exact ciphers. If there's any mismatch we'll provide a shim.
[05:39] Jamal Price: If we run a Dedicated instance with reserved GPUs, does that change the keying model?
[05:45] Sam Collins: Dedicated compute doesn't change the model — it just gives you isolated runtime pools. The connector pattern still applies; dedicated pools can be placed in regions you choose to meet residency.
[05:58] Dr. Lena Ortiz: What about backups and snapshots — we can't have plaintext in snapshots.
[06:02] Priya Nair: Snapshots are encrypted with storage keys; by default they're service-managed but we can switch to customer-managed keys for snapshot encryption as well. When using customer-managed keys, snapshots are encrypted with keys that only you control.
[06:18] Marcus Hale: What's the recommended key rotation process end-to-end? we want minimal downtime and verifiable rollforward.
[06:25] Sam Collins: Typical flow: 1) Generate new key (or version) in your KMS/HSM; 2) Push new wrapping key metadata to Redwood (or Redwood polls); 3) Redwood performs staged rollout — new data keys are used for new sessions, old sessions continue to use old DEKs until TTL expires; 4) After all old sessions complete, retire old key version. We can provide runbooks and automation hooks for zero-downtime rotation.
[06:52] Jamal Price: If we do a pilot, can we start with a read-only unwrap to validate metrics before allowing production unwraps?
[06:58] Priya Nair: Yes — we can set the connector in a dry-run/audit-only mode where Redwood requests unwraps but your connector returns a simulated response and logs the event. Good way to validate logging and performance.
[07:14] Sofia Nguyen: Any legal exposure if Redwood has logs that show key usage even if they don't hold keys? We need to phrase data processing agreement carefully.
[07:21] Sam Collins: We'll work with legal. Our position is we process encrypted payloads and do not have access to plaintext when you use on-prem HSM. The audit logs we store are metadata-level (operation, key id) rather than payload. We'll supply contract language to reflect that.
[07:37] Marcus Hale: About residency, we have EU telemetry that must never leave the Frankfurt region — can Redwood shard logs regionally?
[07:44] Priya Nair: Yes, regional shard placement is supported in Private deployments and Dedicated. For hosted, we can route EU customers to Frankfurt region; for strict residency you'll want a Private/VPC deployment.
[07:58] Jamal Price: Are there any third-party vendors in the control plane path we should worry about?
[08:03] Sam Collins: Third-party contractors are limited. Our control plane is multi-tenant but we have strict access controls and SSO + RBAC enforced, and we can provide the list of subprocessors in the compliance pack.
[08:18] Dr. Lena Ortiz: For SSO we use SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning — can Redwood integrate for audit identity mapping?
[08:25] Sam Collins: Yes, we support SAML and SCIM. We map principals in audit events to your SAML identities, including group claims for RBAC.
[08:36] Marcus Hale: What about long-term retention of logs? we have a 7-year retention policy for certain flight logs.
[08:41] Priya Nair: Redwood's retention defaults are shorter but we offer extended retention as an enterprise add-on. For compliance we can push logs to your archive (S3 with Object Lock) and maintain the retention policy on your side.
[08:58] Jamal Price: Any gotchas with HSM firmware updates or failover? we need high availability and controlled patch windows.
[09:05] Priya Nair: HSM failover is supported — connector can be configured with primary and secondary endpoints. For firmware updates, you control the HSM lifecycle, and Redwood will coordinate around maintenance windows to avoid surprise disconnects.
[09:22] Dr. Lena Ortiz: On the topic of key escrow — we want an escrow for disaster recovery but with multi-sig escrow holding. Is that possible?
[09:30] Sam Collins: We don't hold escrow keys by default. For escrow we can recommend an approach with a third-party escrow vendor or a multi-party HSM arrangement where multiple corporate officers sign. We can bake that into the contract.
[09:45] Marcus Hale: Can you explain the difference between your BYOK and customer-managed key store?
[09:50] Priya Nair: BYOK typically means you provide a wrapping key (public part or wrapped key material) and Redwood unwraps within the runtime; customer-managed key store, especially with HSM connector, means unwrap happens in your environment and Redwood never holds the plaintext key.
[10:06] Jamal Price: Do you support TPM attestation on runtime nodes to prove integrity of the runtime before you provide keys?
[10:12] Sam Collins: Yes, attestation is supported on Private deployments. We can require attestation tokens from nodes before they receive unwrapped keys. For hosted, we have internal attestation but can't expose TPM-level quotes to customers today — worth discussing for an enterprise contract.
[10:30] Dr. Lena Ortiz: For auditability, can we get a periodic signed statement of key usage? like a monthly signed digest?
[10:36] Sam Collins: Yes, we can provide signed monthly digests and raw audit exports to your SIEM.
[10:44] Sofia Nguyen: If we need contractual indemnity for key compromise due to Redwood bug, is that standard?
[10:49] Sam Collins: Redwood provides enterprise indemnity clauses; the specifics depend on the deployment and shared responsibility model. We'll have legal follow up.
[10:59] Marcus Hale: Let's talk about a pilot timeline. We want to test HSM connector performance and logging, then run a small production canary. What's realistic?
[11:06] Priya Nair: A two-week connector pilot plus one week of analysis is typical. If we coordinate quickly we can start pilot by mid-November.
[11:16] Jamal Price: Good. For the pilot, we'll need a step-by-step runbook and a list of metrics to collect.
[11:21] Sam Collins: We'll produce a pilot runbook: metrics include unwrap latency, request success rate, audit event counts, error types, and key rotation behavior.
[11:33] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Anything else we should consider?
[11:36] Marcus Hale: One more — cross-border transfer rules. If an engineer outside EU sometimes pulls logs for debugging, how do we control that?
[11:43] Priya Nair: RBAC + IP / geo guards can limit access; audit trails will show who accessed logs. We can integrate with your SSO and conditional access to block cross-border access if needed.
[11:58] Sam Collins: All right, quick recap and commitments: we'll send the HSM network diagram and port matrix, Priya drafts the pilot runbook, Jamal shares key policy snippets, Sofia confirms legal escrow constraints, and we schedule the on-site workshop week of Nov 15.
[12:20] Marcus Hale: That sounds good, appreciate it.
[12:24] Sofia Nguyen: Thanks everyone.
[12:26] Sam Collins: Thanks — we'll follow up with the deck and compliance pack (NDA first).

End of call.
